change_summary: PLOS ONE has issued an Expression of Concern on this paper. It notes a possible discontinuity in the Fig. 4 LSD1 blot and says Fig. 7 does not match its legend and text, so the H460 LSD1 siRNA migration result is unsupported. It also says the control details are too thin to replicate the transfection experiments and that similarities with other groups' work call the results' validity and provenance into question. The authors did not respond, so the issues are unresolved.
evaluation: Your draft cites Lv et al. [12] in Section 3 (Rationale for Aim 2) for the H460 LSD1 siRNA scratch-assay result, which you call the clearest indication that LSD1 drives migration. The Expression of Concern says Fig. 7 reports no LSD1 siRNA data, so that result is not supported, and this use is directly touched. Your Background (Section 2) also cites [12] for the tissue and survival findings. The notice does not single these out, but it questions the reported results in general, so that use is uncertain. Overall the impact is medium, because your central rationale leans on the affected result, though your plan adds new experiments.
recommendation: Hedge or replace the Section 3 citation, because the notice says Fig. 7 reports no LSD1 siRNA data, so the H460 result the draft takes as its clearest indication is not supported. Also soften the Section 2 citation, since the notice says similarities with other groups' work call the reported results into question, and don't build new work on this paper.

alerts.reason: An expression of concern about figures, data support and provenance puts the findings in doubt. It is not a retraction, and the issues are unresolved because the authors did not respond.

evidence.quote: The results shown in Fig. 7 do not correspond to the description in the Figure legend or the corresponding text of the Results section.
In Fig. 4, when levels are adjusted to visualize background, there appears to be a vertical discontinuity in the LSD1 panel between the 293T and A549 lanes.
Similarities were noted between this article [1] and work by other research groups which call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results.
The authors did not respond or could not be reached to discuss these issues.
